text:
maria_suarez: Hey team — hitting 401 invalid_api_key from hosted API after our SSO rollout. We were using a dev convenience of storing the apikey in a cookie named `redwood_key`, but since SSO the cookie now contains a JWT. Fetch from the browser fails, curl from terminal works. Anyone seen cookie/header precedence weirdness?

support-bot: Ticket created: #SUP-10234 — adding support-engineer.

liam: @maria_suarez can you paste the failing request (browser) and a working curl? Also which endpoint and region?

maria_suarez: endpoint: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat, region: hosted-us. Failing fetch:
```
fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({model: 'rwd-4k', input: 'hi'})
})
```
Note: we were relying on `redwood_key` cookie to be read by our dev proxy and forwarded as Authorization header. After SSO cookie swap the cookie value is a long JWT (contains dots) and server returns 401.

oliver: Do you see an Authorization header in the browser request? Browsers won't auto-turn cookies into headers. Is your proxy doing that?

maria_suarez: yep our dev proxy had a small script that took cookie value and set `Authorization: Bearer <cookie>`. The proxy logs show it forwarded a header, but server logs show `auth: parse_api_key: invalid format` and `auth: token_kind=unknown` for that request id. CLI curl with the same header works:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_XXXX" -d '{"model":"rwd-4k","input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
```
works fine. The failing header contains the JWT (looks like `eyJhbGciOi... . ...`) which our edge treats as not an api key -> 401.

liam: Huh. So the header arrives but value is a JWT, not an API key. Why would your proxy pick up the SSO cookie rather than the dashboard API key? Did the cookie name collide?

maria_suarez: yes — our cookie name was `redwood_key`. SSO set a cookie with the same name on the domain, overwriting it. We missed that when enabling SSO.

oliver: That explains it. Edge auth currently validates header format and expects `sk_` prefix for hosted keys; a JWT won't match. The 401 is valid. Two ways to mitigate: (1) change cookie name / remove SSO cookie in dev, (2) update proxy to prefer explicit header input rather than reading cookie. Workaround: set header client-side with the dashboard key (not cookie).

liam: For longer-term, I'll open an infra task to make the edge log clearer when cookie-derived headers are non-apikey tokens, and add a diagnostic response code and human message. Also adding a doc note about cookie-name collisions during SSO rollouts.

maria_suarez: thanks. Quick ask — can support temporarily whitelist our org so requests containing dashboard keys still succeed while we fix dev env?\/ Not ideal but would help demo today.

oliver: I can't change auth policy for hosted, but we can request an exception from security. I'll escalate to security with reproduction steps and request a temporary bypass for your org's test subdomain.

liam: Filed infra issue INFRA-6123 to: prefer Authorization header over cookie-derived header when both exist; emit clear error message on token format mismatch; add debugging hint `hint: cookie name collision with SSO?`. Assigning to eng-runtime.

maria_suarez: perfect — temporary workaround for anyone hitting this: clear the `redwood_key` cookie or rename your dev cookie to `rw_dev_key` and set `Authorization: Bearer <sk_...>` explicitly. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Updating ticket #SUP-10234 — linked INFRA-6123 and security escalation.

liam: tagging @eng-oncall to prioritize if this affects more customers.

oliver: security replied — accepted risk assessment for a temporary org-scoped exception while customer fixes config; working through audit log requirements.

maria_suarez: thanks all, will update once we rename cookie and confirm behaves.

liam: follow-up: we'll also add a short FAQ entry in docs about avoiding `redwood_*` cookie names to prevent collisions with SSO/dashboard cookies.

maria_suarez: confirmed — clearing the cookie fixed the browser request immediately. No more 401. Closing on my side once docs/info live.
